title: Stalk borer in maize and sorghum - Zambia

Header: Stalk borer in maize and sorghum - Zambia
Busseola fusca African maize stalk borer

Prevention: Plough, slash, disk and/ or harrow stems and stubbles after harvest.
This breaks the stems and exposes the caterpillars to natural enemies and extreme weather.
It limits the pest in the following season's crops.
Destroy alternate hosts, like wild sorghum, to reduce stalk borers.
Rotate with legumes, but do not rotate between maize, millet and sorghum.
Lines of holes in leaves made by the stalk borer. (Source:
Monitoring: Monitor from 3 weeks after planting onwards.
Inspect two times per week until the plants flower.
The first signs of stalk borer attack are small holes or 'window pane damage' in straight lines across the newest leaves of maize or sorghum.
Check for white-yellowish larvae with a grey tinge or pinkish colour.
The threshold for stalk borers is when 10% of plants show damage symptoms.
Look for holes in stems and dead hearts.
It's difficult to control the stalk borers in the later stages because larvae are protected when they bore into stalks.
Direct Control: Apply ash or dry soil, by putting one teaspoon of ash or soil into the leaf funnel of young plants.
Too much soil or ash can damage the leaf.
Ash or soil should be used before the appearance of any symptoms.
This means when stalk borers are known in the area or the last cropping season.
Apply neem-based product, e.g. nimbicidine (50-60ml/16L) in whorls.
Apply 25-50g of neem cake powder diluted per litre water, into the leaf funnel.
Sprays may need to be repeated after 10 to 14 days until flowering.
Spray onto the leaf sheath funnels of young leaves immediately after preparation.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, pre-harvest interval, max. number of sprays, and restricted re-entry interval.
Do not empty into drains and water sources.
Always consult recent list of registered pesticides of
Usually applied at 2.5ml/100m row in 3 litres water, but double- check labels.
Should be applied to young plants, particularly onto leaf sheath funnels.
Pyrethroid group of insecticides with contact activity.
PHI 14 days; REI 7 days after spray; max. 2 sprays per season.
Do not apply to plants suffering from drought stress.
Do not contaminate surface waters or ditches.
High risk to nearly all beneficial insects like pollinators and predators.
